chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'I enter with these people in the Maghrib prayer, and they hasten me so that I do not have time to call the adhan or iqamah, and I do not recite anything except Al-Hamd (Surah Al-Fatiha) until they bow. Will that suffice for me?' He said, 'Yes, Al-Hamd alone will suffice for you.' And it is also possible that the report covers the state of taqiyya (dissimulation), because if the state is one of taqiyya and fear, and the person does not catch up with the recitation with them, it is permissible for him to leave the recitation and rely on that prayer after he has caught the ruku' (bowing). And that which reveals what we mentioned is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I only recite Surah Al-Fatiha before the Imam bows in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the sufficiency of reciting only Surah Al-Fatiha for a latecomer who joins the Maghrib prayer and catches the imam's bowing (*ruku'*). While the ruling is general, the text highlights its particular relevance to *taqiyya* (dissimulation) or fear, where practical constraints might prevent full recitation, thereby validating the prayer's validity based on the essential act of joining the congregation in *ruku'*. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the core validity of the prayer is maintained through the physical participation in the imam's movements when recitation is abbreviated.
